subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned agentic memory flush before explicit and implicit session rollover, and what default/security boundary should it use?
rationale: The source proves the requested gap is real, but the fix changes session lifecycle behavior, silent agent execution, memory writes, latency, and plugin boundaries; automation cannot choose those product and security tradeoffs safely.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core design
options.body: Add a reset-lifecycle memory flush contract covering `/new`, `/reset`, daily, and idle rollover with explicit timeout, sandbox, consent, and failure semantics.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Leave core rollover behavior unchanged and instead extend/document plugin hooks so memory plugins can implement pre-reset persistence without a core agent turn.

options.title: Limit to mechanical preservation
options.body: Copy or expose existing compaction summaries and raw transcript data across reset while deferring agentic turns to a separate memory-system design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core design
recommendation.body: Add a reset-lifecycle memory flush contract covering `/new`, `/reset`, daily, and idle rollover with explicit timeout, sandbox, consent, and failure semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the pre-compaction flush, `/new` reset behavior, and the merged reset-hook feature history, making him the best available routing owner for the product boundary.
